classification.text_en: The Quran names horses (al-khayl) with mules and donkeys, and among the desires made attractive to people it names marked horses (al-khayl al-musawwamah).

origin.note_en: The Quran does not describe the origin of the horse in particular.

purpose.text_en: Horses, mules and donkeys are named for people to ride and as adornment. People are told to prepare strength including tethered horses to deter the enemy of God.

nature.note_en: The Quran does not describe the horse beyond its uses.

abilities.note_en: The Quran does not describe abilities of the horse.

limitations.note_en: The Quran does not describe limits of the horse.

relationship_with_humans.text_en: Love of marked horses, with other desires, is made attractive to people as the enjoyment of worldly life. They are also named for riding and as readiness against an enemy.

quranic_events.text_en: Horses appear in a verse on spoils for which the believers had not driven any horse or riding beast. Iblis is also told to rally against people with his horse and foot.

chronological_position.note_en: The Quran gives no time or order for the horse.

location.note_en: The Quran does not say where horses live.

misconceptions.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the Quran mentions horses for riding, adornment and readiness. It describes no breed or feature, and the surah of the runners (al-'Adiyat) swears by 'the runners' without naming the animal.

lessons.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the same animals appear as enjoyment and as readiness, which is read as a lesson that gifts carry both pleasure and responsibility.

vocabulary.text_en: Words used: al-khayl (horses), ribat al-khayl (tethered horses), al-musawwamah (marked), al-rikab (riding beasts), khaylika wa rajilika (your horse and your foot).
